subject: Renewal: usage-led stability & top-up proposal

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@acme.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — dedicated sizing questions

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for the Dedicated pool is up in early December (contract attached on our side). Over the last three months we’ve seen bursts in inference traffic for our chat assistants that pushed utilization to 88% p95 and produced a number of queuing events during peak windows.

Before we sign anything I want to understand the least-risk approach to avoid throttles during our holiday peak. Specifically:
- What’s your recommended delta between steady-state commit and observed peak?
- How do you suggest we structure burst vs reserved so we don’t pay for idle headroom but also don’t hit request failures?

Can we hop on a 30 min call next week to walk through options? I can bring our infra lead if it helps.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
CTO, Acme AI
E: evan.brooks@acme.ai
T: +1 (415) 555-0198

P.S. I attached our internal usage export for Q3 — thought it might be useful. (attachment: acme-usage-summary-2026Q3.csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — dedicated sizing questions

Evan — thanks for the context and the CSV, that helps.

Short answers up front:
- Baseline guidance: aim for a reserved commit ~15% above median steady-state traffic and a burst pool sized to absorb observed p95 peaks (or ~10–20 GPUs depending on model family).
- Hybrid approach: reserved commit + burst pool + autoscale with pre-warmed slots gives the best balance between cost and availability.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll run a quick utilization analysis (I attached the cleaned summary).
2) Internal alignment: loop in CS and SE to size burst and the commit uplift precisely.
3) I’ll send a short amendment with two alternatives (conservative and cost-optimized) and an expected cost delta.

Available next week: Mon/Tue 10–12 PST. What works for you?

Regards,
Jordan Blake

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — dedicated sizing questions

Forwarding Acme’s note + CSV. They hit 88% p95 during peaks and want a low-risk renewal path. I’m proposing we prepare two formal options for them:

Option A — Stability-first (recommended for holiday peak):
- Reserved commit: current commit + 15% (covers steady growth)
- Burst pool: +12 GPUs (pre-warmed + autoscale to 25% additional headroom)
- Canary rollout for model variant and KV cache warm-up window
- Runbook: 2-hour escalation SLA, auto-fallback to smaller model variant if queue > threshold

Option B — Cost-optimized:
- Reserved commit: current commit + 7%
- Burst pool: +6 GPUs, aggressive burst throttling with queued requests 
- Enable quantization suggestions and prefix caching to reduce token cost

Questions for SE/Operations:
- Ben, can you validate that +12 GPUs at their observed seq_len distribution will reduce p95 queuing?
- Mina, what pricing uplift would a 90-day top-up amendment look like vs an annual commit increase?

Attachments I’m sending to the customer after internal sign-off: proposed-amendment-commits.pdf, runbook-surge-handling.md

Timeline: want to get a recommended option to Acme by Mon 2026-11-16 so they can review with procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — dedicated sizing questions

Jordan / team — quick SE notes:

- With their sequence length distribution (median 128, p95 ~ 1024) the biggest wins are pre-warmed KV caches and continuous batching tweaks during peak minutes. +12 GPUs will materially reduce queuing, but the exact number depends on the mix of chat vs embedding workloads.
- Recommendation: provision +8 GPUs as reserved buffer (short-term commit) and expose +6 extra as burst that can spin up with 60–90s warm-up. That hybrid gets them to ~95% of peak headroom while keeping committed cost lower.
- Kernel/quantization note: if they accept an int8 path for non-critical models we can drop per-token cost ~18% and translate that into fewer GPUs required equivalently.
- Canary plan: stage half the burst on a dedicated AZ to validate kernel behavior under 2x load.

I’ll draft pricing assumptions to feed Mina’s amendment. Also flag for infra: we’ll need the KV pre-warm hook enabled next Friday to validate under synthetic traffic.

-Ben

ben_carter@redwood.com

Evan — thanks again for the call last Friday. We reviewed your Q3 usage and modeled several renewal tracks. Below is our recommended path and the alternative.

Recommended (Stability-first) — "90-day top-up + smoothing":
- Reserved commit: current commit + 10% (short-term uplift to avoid over-commit)
- 90-day top-up burst pool: +12 GPUs (pre-warmed, autoscale with 60s warm-up)
- Observability: per-route token/latency charts + alert thresholds for p95 queuing
- Runbook + SLA: 2-hour incident response, automated fallback to smaller model variant under sustained queueing
- Estimated ARR uplift vs current: ~9.6% (detailed numbers in attached amendment)

Alternative (Cost-optimized):
- Reserved commit: current commit + 5%
- Burst pool: +6 GPUs, enable int8 for non-prod models which reduces token cost ~18%
- Estimated ARR uplift: ~4.2%

Attachments: proposed-amendment-commits.pdf (detailed pricing), runbook-surge-handling.md, acme-renewal-amendment-2026.docx
